comments.author: GeekyBear
comments.story: Lenovo announces the first Arm-based ThinkPad
comments.why: Test of x86 software compatibility on ARM Windows.
comments.text: Has Windows gotten any better at running x86-64 Windows software on ARM hardware? The last time I saw this tested, it was more likely to fail than succeed, but it's been a while. [VIDEO]

comments.author: GeekyBear
comments.story: Dropbox Sync does not natively support Apple Silicon
comments.why: x64 emulation performed poorly on Surface hardware.
comments.text: They introduced x64 64 bit emulation in the Dev channel several months ago, but it didn't work well at all. It also was more performant running in a VM on last year's MacBook Air than running natively on Microsoft's flagship hardware. [VIDEO]

comments.author: GeekyBear
comments.story: Samsung to jump into laptop processor market with Exynos chip in H2
comments.why: Shows how far behind Qualcomm is.
comments.text: Samsung's custom cores haven't been competitive with Qualcomm so far, much less Apple. You only have to look at comparisons between the Surface Pro X and the M1 Macbook Air to see how far behind Qualcomm is. [VIDEO]

comments.author: pmarreck
comments.story: M1 MacBook Air hits 900 GFlops in the browser with Safari's experimental WebGPU
comments.why: Windows not yet ready for ARM versus Apple.
comments.text: The raving in this thread is to me indicative of how far behind Intel has fallen behind ARM in technical terms. Now we just need more, better, faster ARM-based chips. Linux is ready, macOS is ready... but it looks like Windows is not yet ready: [VIDEO]

comments.story: Asahi Linux: Linux on Apple Silicon project
comments.why: Surface Pro X versus M1 MacBook Air comparison.
comments.text: Linus Tech Tips actually just released a video a couple of hours ago where they compared the Surface Pro X SQ2 with the M1 MacBook Air. It was not pretty. [VIDEO]

comments.author: GeekyBear
comments.story: Asahi Linux: Linux on Apple Silicon project
comments.why: Windows x86-64 emulation on ARM has compatibility issues.
comments.text: Legacy x86-64 app emulation has only just appeared in alpha form and still has massive compatibility issues. I'd still call it something we hope to see in the future, instead of a working proof of concept. [VIDEO]
